clue.text: Driver alert and detects spin

parts.note: to rumble someone is to find them out, so detects means rumbles
a spin is a short outing, a trip

explanation.surface: A gadget that warns a motorist and also spots skids or spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged bands on a road edge make tyres vibrate noisily, warning an inattentive motorist.

clue.text: Second-in-command in a tub at sea that's rarely afloat

indicators.note: the chosen letter goes inside the jumbled letters, so in signals insertion
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of a tub are rearranged
the second letter of the word command is taken, hence the hyphenated phrase

explanation.surface: A deputy aboard some tub of a vessel that hardly ever stays on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-in-command' looks like a naval rank, but splits as the second letter of 'command' (O) going 'in' UBAT, the anagram of A TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine spends most of its time submerged, so it is something seldom floating on top.

clue.text: Unruly class's inappropriate behaviour

parts.note: an unruly child is a bad one
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A disorderly schoolroom behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad form is an idiom for conduct that breaks social conventions, i.e. improper manners.

clue.text: One who sings the praises of European Union record is essentially nutty

parts.note: a log is a written record
taken as written

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre, so the middle letter of nutty is taken

explanation.surface: A fan of the EU whose recorded views are basically crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who delivers a eulogy speaks in high praise of a person, so they sing that person's praises.

clue.text: Rising politician's no unknown, and on a roll

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, so the word is reversed
no means without, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: An ambitious politician who knows everything and is on a winning streak.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is a list of names, and a duty roster is such a list.

clue.text: Worcester Conference chief?

parts.note: Conference is a well-known British variety of pear
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: Who heads a conference held in the city of Worcester?
explanation.walkthrough: Worcester and Conference look like a place and a meeting; both are fruit varieties.
explanation.definitionFit: The Worcester Pearmain is an English apple variety, so Worcester names it by its first word.

clue.text: Popular runny brie devoured in boozer

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: runny cheese loses its shape, so the letters of brie are rearranged

parts.note: ate means devoured

explanation.surface: A well-liked runny brie is wolfed down in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' looks like a pub, a British slang sense, but it is a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drunkard can be called a boozer, a noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Hull City ref fixed a match for money

indicators.note: a fixed match is rigged, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A referee at Hull City football club rigged a game for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is a jocular or disapproving idiom for cash, especially dishonestly gained.

clue.text: Piccalilli unnecessarily filling rolls causing dissatisfaction

indicators.note: rolls means the hidden letters turn over and read backwards
the letters sit inside the words like a sandwich filling

explanation.surface: Pickle needlessly stuffed into bread rolls leaves the eater unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' looks like bread but tells you to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a weary discontent with things.

clue.text: Providing comfort with US apartment on loan

parts.note: condo is American for a condominium flat
something on loan has been lent

explanation.surface: An American flat lent out free, a comforting arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Condolent is an adjective for expressing sympathy, consoling someone grieving.

clue.text: Tab or container of cola tipped into tumbler

indicators.note: tipped over means the whole string is turned around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the outside letters of cola contain the rest

explanation.surface: A soft drink or can of cola poured into a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbler' looks like a drinking glass but is a gymnast; Tab is a diet cola brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is one who performs somersaults and handsprings, a circus gymnast.

clue.text: Ultimately government run in tune with European Right will be more powerful

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the tune word

parts.note: a song is a tune

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of government

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A government in harmony with Europe's right wing will gain power.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: stronger means having greater force or power.

clue.text: Uncommunicative No. 10 is source of hearsay

parts.note: in rugby union the stand-off half, or fly-half, wears the number 10 shirt
taken as written

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so the first letter of hearsay

explanation.surface: Downing Street is tight-lipped, yet it is where rumours originate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 10' suggests Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence, but is a rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof and unsociable keeps others at a distance and says little.

clue.text: Around east stormy petrel is abounding

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the other one
stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters of petrel are shaken up

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A storm petrel circling in the east, a seabird that is plentiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means well filled or abundantly supplied, so teeming or abounding.

clue.text: Balance of online feature

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail, so it means online
a quality is a feature or characteristic

explanation.surface: Fairness as one aspect of the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Equality is evenness or parity between things, a state of balance.

clue.text: A restraint in architectural style

parts.note: a dam restrains water

explanation.surface: Restraint shown in the style of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam brothers gave their name to a neoclassical style of Georgian architecture and interiors.

clue.text: Shy relative?

parts.note: shy also means to throw, and this fairground target is a figure with a family title that people throw things at

explanation.walkthrough: Shy reads as timid, but means a throw; Aunt Sally is a British pub and fairground game of throwing sticks at a target, and a figure of easy criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: The target in the throwing game is named for an aunt, hence a family member one has a shy at.

clue.text: Cheese souffle tip's slant nothing new

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a tilt is a slant
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cheese souffle's top leans over and isn't fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a famous English blue cheese, an example of the category.

clue.text: Without oxygen second muscle may become insubstantial

indicators.note: without means the named element is left out

parts.note: the pectoral is a chest muscle
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Deprived of oxygen, a muscle soon grows weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectral means ghostly, and a ghost is something without solid substance.

clue.text: Special identity adopted by peripheral misfit

indicators.note: being adopted means being taken in, so these letters go inside

parts.note: outer means peripheral, on the edge
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A distinctive persona taken on by someone on the fringe who doesn't fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider is someone who does not belong to a group, a person out of place.

clue.text: Compact car?

parts.note: compact here means shortened: the clipped name of a German luxury marque

explanation.walkthrough: A compact car is a small model, but here the car's name itself is compacted: Merc is short for Mercedes.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is the informal shortening of Mercedes, so it is the car brand in condensed form.

clue.text: Yours truly first, Farah second! One on top of rostrum is shortly making history

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
Mo Farah is the British Olympic distance runner
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: is shortened to the contraction 's leaves just the S

explanation.surface: An athletics podium: me first, Farah second, one on top, making history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' and 'second' merely order the pieces, ME then MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoirs are a written account of one's own life, a personal history.

clue.text: Jumped ahead of field in unfashionable gymnastics

indicators.note: in signals the field word is placed inside

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
PT is physical training, school gymnastics
a lea is a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A gymnast vaults clear of the field in an old-fashioned routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To outleap someone is to jump further or higher than them, getting ahead.

clue.text: Group of musicians in matching clothes

definitions.meaning: a band of players performing together
an outfit of garments designed to be worn together

explanation.surface: A band all dressed in the same outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a set of things acting together, whether players in a band or coordinated garments.

clue.text: Girl I may get a drink in Indian restaurant

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl orders a drink at an Indian restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is a yoghurt drink served with Indian meals.

clue.text: Furious fellow controlled show of nerves

parts.note: to run a business is to control it
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: An angry man in charge reveals his nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means wild with emotion or frenzied activity, so furious in the sense of fierce haste.

clue.text: Endive or last of celery missing with it

indicators.note: missing means the following letters are absent

parts.note: chicory is another name for endive
taken as written

indicators.note: points to the final letter of celery

explanation.surface: A salad of endive, or celery, missing something to go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' is a definition meaning trendy, not a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it means being fashionable and up to date, i.e. stylish.

clue.text: Primary principal previously precipitate

indicators.note: previously means the head word comes before the other one

parts.note: a head is the principal of a school
first means primary

explanation.surface: A primary school headteacher acting rashly before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, the hyphenated word means rash and hasty, rushing in like plunging in.

clue.text: Music that might waft from a boat?

definitions.text: that might waft from a boat?
definitions.meaning: a gravy or sauce boat holds sauce, whose aroma might drift up from it

explanation.surface: Latin rhythms drifting over the water from a passing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The boat is not a vessel on water but a sauce boat for serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is both a lively Latin dance music and a spicy Mexican sauce.

clue.text: Tip off ace result about joint academic post

indicators.note: about suggests moving letters around, so they are rearranged
tip off means the first letter of ace is removed

parts.note: taken as written
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A warning about a winning serve gets a smoky joint passed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal: CE (ace minus its tip) and RESULT are rearranged into LECTURES.
explanation.definitionFit: A university position as a lecturer is a teaching appointment in academia.
